actual_target_quantifiers.M1: Fix divisor exponent e, polynomial-location exponent Kloc and delta>0 before x,I,r,q. I lies in [-x^Kloc,x^Kloc], length<=L<=x^Kloc, q is a POSITIVE integer with q<=L*x^(-delta), and r is ANY residue. Sum_{t in I,t=r modq,t!=0}tau(|t|)^e << (L/q)*tau(q)^e*log(x)^O(e,Kloc,delta). No coprime(r,q) assumption; gcd reduction is part of its proof.
actual_target_quantifiers.M2: Fix R,S,C0,Kloc,delta before x,a,r,q and interval J subset[1,C0*x]. Uniformly for polynomially bounded signed a and all positive q<=x^(1-delta), sum_{v in J,v=r modq,v!=a}tau(v)^R*tau(|v-a|)^S << (x/q)*tau(q)^O(R,S)*log(x)^O(R,S,Kloc,delta). Neither (a,q)=1 nor r=a is required. Constants and threshold precede all those varying parameters. There is no tau(a) factor.
actual_target_quantifiers.rough_factor_role: The actual non-q1 use in the bottom audit is f|m while removing (m,r2)>1, so v=mn1 is 0 mod f. An active r2 is primitive to a; hence its common factor f is also coprime to a. Consequently v-a is -a mod f, a primitive nonzero class, not a multiple of f. The required f range is f<=O(M)<=O(x^(1-delta)), after a smaller fixed delta. The second 1/f from this mean combines with an outer modulus 1/f to make the rough tail sum tau(f)^O/f^2. It is NOT assumed f<=x^kappa.

It does not even have an arbitrary residue-r argument. q=0 leaves no product terms after v!=a and is a finite empty case, not an x/q estimate. The actual p carrier is primitive to a, but an arbitrary auxiliary q in this draft is not. minimal_next_lemma.name: strict_floor_E1_progression_payment
minimal_next_lemma.notation: d_k(n)=fouvryTau k n. k>=2, q>=1 are integers; r is any integer; 1<=A<=B<=Z, Z>=2 are real; Y=B-A; S is ANY finite set of natural n with A<=n<=B and n=r modq. D=floor(Z^(1-1/k)). g_d=gcd(d,q), and compatibility g_d|r is integer divisibility.
minimal_next_lemma.exact_finite_type: For every such k,q,r,A,B,Z,S, sum_{n in S}d_k(n) <= k * sum_{1<=d<=D, g_d|r} d_(k-1)(d) * (Y*g_d/(d*q)+1).
minimal_next_lemma.uniform_closed_consequence: sum_{n in S}d_k(n) <= k * [(Y/q)*d_k(q)*(1+log Z)^(k-1) + Z^(1-1/k)*(1+log Z)^(k-2)]. If gcd(r,q)=1, replace d_k(q) in the main term by1. The remainder is NOT divided by q.
complete_proof: StrictFloor's largest-coordinate cover gives d_k(n)<=k*sum_{d|n,1<=d<=D}d_(k-1)(d) for every n<=Z. The strict successor inequality at the true floor is exactly its existing premise; no floor-to-ceiling alteration is needed. Exchange these finite sums.

For d|n and n=r modq, necessarily g_d|r. If compatible, any two such n differ by lcm(d,q)=d*q/g_d; hence within [A,B] there are at most Y*g_d/(d*q)+1. This follows by ordering the points, or mapping one chosen point to integer multiples of the spacing. It does not require proving existence of a CRT representative. Empty incompatible fibers contribute zero. This proves the exact finite type.

Write j=k-1. The weighted main sum is at most sum_{d<=D}d_j(d)*gcd(d,q)/d. Since gcd(d,q)<=sum_{g|q,g|d}g, this is <=sum_{g|q}g*sum_{u<=D/g}d_j(g*u)/(g*u). Use d_j(g*u)<=d_j(g)d_j(u), then the existing harmonic divisor bound, to obtain <=(1+log Z)^j*sum_{g|q}d_j(g)=d_k(q)*(1+log Z)^j. The submultiplicative inequality follows prime by prime: split any weak composition of e+f deterministically into one of e and one of f; the pair recombines uniquely. If gcd(r,q)=1, all compatible d have gcd(d,q)=1, and the main weighted sum is simply bounded by the harmonic mean without d_k(q).

Drop compatibility from the nonnegative +1 sum. The existing ordinary mean gives sum_{d<=D}d_(k-1)(d)<=D*(1+log Z)^(k-2), with D<=Z^(1-1/k). This proves the closed consequence. Singleton/zero-length intervals are covered by the +1 remainder.

quotient_case_v_equals_a_modq.exact_reindex: For q>=1 and v!=a in v=a modq, t=|v-a|=q*u with positive integer u. The maps on v>a and v<a are injective, with multiplicity at most2 in their union. For v in an interval of length Y, each u image is supported in a positive real interval of length<=Y/q and upper endpoint<=Z/q if |v-a|<=Z. Use Zq=max(2,Z/q) for E1. Never use tau(0).
quotient_case_v_equals_a_modq.single_shifted_moment: For e fixed, k>=max(2,2^e), sum tau(|v-a|)^e <= 2*k*tau(q)^e*[(Y/q)*(1+log Zq)^(k-1)+Zq^(1-1/k)*(1+log Zq)^(k-2)]. tau(q*u)<=tau(q)*tau(u) has been paid explicitly. The factor2 merely allows both signs.
quotient_case_v_equals_a_modq.absorption_range: When Y is O(x), Z is O(x^(1+kappa)), q<=x, the quotient remainder is absorbed by x/q whenever q<=x^(1-kappa*(k-1)), up to fixed endpoint constants in the final bound: (x^(1+kappa)/q)^(1-1/k)<=x/q is equivalent to q<=x^(1-kappa*(k-1)). For a general polynomial location x^Kloc, this range is q<=x^(k-Kloc*(k-1)); it can be empty even at q=1. This is not automatically the manuscript range.
quotient_case_v_equals_a_modq.literal_fold_partial_corollary: Let k=262144, w(t)=tau(t)*d4(t)^4, L=1+log x. There exists an absolute fixed C*>0 before x,kappa,a,q such that for every x>=2, 0<=kappa<=1/(2*k), signed integer a with |a|<=x^(1+kappa), and positive integer q<=x^(1/4), sum_{0<v<=floor(6*x),v!=a,v=a modq}tau(v)*w(|v-a|) <= C* (x/q)*w(q)*sqrt(d4(q))*L^131073. If gcd(a,q)=1, remove sqrt(d4(q)). Thus a coarser general modulus factor tau(q)^15, or tau(q)^13 in the primitive case, suffices. These are partial-range conclusions, not general M2 or a new outsideEnergy theorem.
quotient_case_v_equals_a_modq.literal_corollary_proof: Cauchy separates tau(v)^2<=d4(v) and w(t)^2<=d_k(t). For the second factor FIRST use w(q*u)<=w(q)w(u), and then w(u)^2<=d_k(u), avoiding the much larger d_k(q) cost. The new progression E1 with order4 bounds the first sum by O(((x/q)*d4(q)+x^(3/4))*L^3), with d4(q) absent when gcd(a,q)=1. Quotient E1 bounds the second by O(w(q)^2*[x/q+(x^(1+kappa)/q)^(1-1/k)+1]*L^(k-1)). For q<=x^(1/4), the first remainder is<=x/q. The second is also<=O(x/q), since the cap gives 1-kappa*(k-1)>=1/2 and q<=x^(1/4). Taking a square root gives log exponent (3+k-1)/2=131073. Finally d4(q)<=tau(q)^3, so w(q)*sqrt(d4(q))<=tau(q)^(29/2)<=tau(q)^15. All constants depend only on the fixed orders and endpoints, not q or a.

why_actual_general_M2_remains.general_residue: For v=r modq, the shifted residue is r-a. After g=gcd(r-a,q), only g divides t, leaving a primitive progression modulo q/g. Dividing by the whole q is false unless r=a modq. The elementary CRT E1 remainder persists on that primitive progression.
why_actual_general_M2_remains.rough_factor_class: For actual v=0 modq and gcd(a,q)=1, the unshifted factor can be divided by q and bounded by an ordinary full-interval divisor mean. But the shifted factor is primitive modq and its E1 remainder is O(x^((1+kappa)*(1-1/k_s))) without 1/q, where k_s is the fixed shifted SECOND-moment order. To absorb it one only gets the sufficient range q<=x^eta, eta=1/k_s-kappa*(1-1/k_s). Under kappa<=1/(2*k_s), q<=x^(1/(2*k_s)) is uniformly sufficient. This tiny fixed power is not the required f<=O(M)<=O(x^(1-delta)). For general polynomial location replace eta by 1-Kloc*(1-1/k_s), which may be nonpositive.
why_actual_general_M2_remains.no_false_impossibility_claim: These bounds show the limitation of THIS E1 proof and these pointwise estimates. They are not a counterexample to M2 and do not prove no other elementary argument could handle the range. Enlarging a progression to all integers forfeits x/q. A pointwise x^epsilon divisor bound is not a substitute for a polylog mean in the rough-tail step: z=x^(1/(loglog x)^3) cannot absorb a fixed x^epsilon.
why_actual_general_M2_remains.true_missing_analysis: To cover the full stated M1/M2 range, the existing elementary package needs an additional primitive short-interval progression argument with average scale L/q down to x^delta, uniformly over polynomially located signed intervals and all reduced residues, plus the explicit gcd/tau(q) factors. The supplied manuscript uses classical Shiu for precisely this range. A proof specialized to the weighted sum over rough f could be an alternative, but its f-dependence and 1/f^2 tail must be proved; neither the new fold nor E1 currently provides it.
why_actual_general_M2_remains.no_claimed_parameter_upgrade: No q<=x^kappa assumption is imposed on the old target. No restriction q<=x^(1/4) or q<=x^(1/(2*k_s)) is silently substituted for its universal q range. The existing capped-kappa local application and the old arbitrary-polynomial-shift theorem remain separate.
